chapter_title: Concerning Four Hunters of Light and Four of Darkness.
chapter_note: This chapter is largely a systematic correspondential teaching: each “hunter” is defined by a stable set of internal mappings (hunter → net/ship/sea) within Manichaean cosmic architecture. The main later intrusions are (a) dialogue frame formulas (“the apostle speaks…”) and (b) cosmos→institution/polemical pointing (“holy church”, “rules in every sect”, “erroneous teaching”), which break the substrate rule that both sides of the mapping remain inside the cosmic system. The beatitude-style closings are pastoral exhortation.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks…”) is compiling-community frame; no cosmological mapping content is expounded here beyond announcing a list.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the First Man who was sent from the greatness. He threw himself down to the five storehouses of Darkness, he caught and siezed the Enmity [... ...] his net also [... ...] out over all the children of Darkness [... ...]. His ship is his four sons who are swathed over his body. The sea is the land of Darkness [... ...]; his net is [...] and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, systematic correspondential exposition: cosmic agent (First Man) mapped to ship/sea/net wholly within the mythic-cosmological system; no audience address or institutional identification.

paragraphs.core_text: The second hunter is the Third Ambassador. This one, for by his light image, which he revealed to the depths below, he hunted after the entire light that is in all things; as it is established in them. His net is his light image, [...] the whole universe and took it prisoner, to this likeness [... His] ship is his light ship. [The sea] is the universe [...] which were hunted after by his net [...] his [glorious] image.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmic mechanics (image-revelation, hunting light from “all things”) and fixed correspondences (net/ship/sea) remain internal to the cosmology; no NT citation formula or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is Jesus the Splendour, who came from the greatness, who hunts after the light and life; and he [...] it to the heights. His net is his wisdom, [the] light wisdom with which he hunts the souls, catching them in the net. The sea is the error of the universe, the law of Sin [...], the souls that are drowning in it [...]. He catches them in his net. They are the souls [... th]em by his light wisdom.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional mapping clause “His ship is his holy church [...]”, because it pivots the correspondential set from cosmos→cosmos into cosmos→church (editorial institutional application).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological entity (“Jesus the Splendour”) presented in the same hunter/net/sea mapping style, but interrupted by an ecclesial identification (“holy church”), indicating later editorial application embedded in the older schematic.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth hunter is the great counsel that [...] that lives in the circuit [...] entire universe in it today. Yet, at the end, in the dissolution of the universe, this very counsel of life will gather itself in and sculpt its soul in the Last Statue. Its net is its Living Spirit, because with its Spirit it can hunt after the light and the life that is in all things; and build it upon its body. Its ship, in which it is established, is this light cloud whereby it itself travels in the five elements [...], the great fire that will burn all the buildings of [... ...] in its net is the light and the life. It can rescue and free it from all bonds and fetters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dense cosmological-process teaching (end-time dissolution, Last Statue, Living Spirit as ‘net’, light cloud/elemental travel, great fire) retains internal cosmic referents; the single temporal adverb “today” does not introduce institutions or direct exhortation.
Beatitude/exhortation to moral perfection and personal escape from punishment; shifts from describing cosmic structure to urging behavior/outcome for the listener.
Explicit structural hinge with dialogue/frame formula (“Once again he speaks… I will also teach you…”), functioning as editorial scaffolding between two lists.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the King of they who belong to the Darkness, who hunted after the living soul with his net at the beginning of the worlds. His net is his fire and his Lust that he has put upon the living soul, with which he has entangled it [...], through all his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-agent description with internal correspondences (net=fire/Lust; target=living soul) and mythic time-marker (“beginning of the worlds”); no institutional polemic or audience address.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second hunter is the evil counsel that lives in [...] that hunts after the light [...] and [...] up from [...] the earths to heaven. It binds them with its powers, which bring them to the heavenly worlds above. Its net is [...] whereby they are drawn up from the abyss [to the heig]hts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systemic cosmological mechanics (binding/drawing light across earths→heavens; abyss→heights) expressed in the same hunter/net schema; stays inside the cosmic geography.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is Lust [...] walks in every power of the flesh that walks [...] in the [...] the living souls [... ...] them in its bodies, which [... ...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Personified cosmic force (Lust) acting as hunter; although anthropological (“flesh”), it remains within the mythic-ontological system rather than identifying contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the remainder (“that rules in every sect… erroneous teaching…”) because it maps the cosmic hunter onto contemporary religious groupings (“every sect”) and institutional/polemical categories (“erroneous teaching”), i.e., cosmos→editorial present.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a plausible substrate-style identification of a cosmic hunter, then immediately pivots to present-world polemic and disciplinary rhetoric, marking a later application layer grafted onto the schema.
Beatitude/exhortation addressed to the hearer (“recognise… through knowledge”), promising salvation; not structural cosmological exposition.
